claim: Fix integers \(H\ge2\), \(s\ge2\), and row occupancies \(1\le r_i\le H\) for \(1\le i\le s\). Independently for each species \(i\), choose a uniformly random \(r_i\)-subset \(A_i\) of the same \(H\) labeled sites. Put \(X_{ij}=|A_i\cap A_j|\), \(G_{ij}=(r_i-X_{ij})(r_j-X_{ij})\), and the classical Stone--Roberts checkerboard score \(C=\binom{s}{2}^{-1}\sum_{i<j}G_{ij}\). For every simple forest \(F\) on the species labels, the random variables \(\{X_{ij}:\{i,j\}\in E(F)\}\) are mutually independent, each having the hypergeometric overlap law. Thus distinct species-pair checkerboard contributions are pairwise independent even when the pairs share a species. With \(t_k(a,b)=\frac{(a)_{\underline{k}}(b)_{\underline{k}}}{(H)_{\underline{k}}}\) for \(0\le k\le H\), \(t_k=0\) for \(k>H\), and \(K=a+b-1\), set \(\mu(a,b)=ab-Kt_1+t_2=\frac{ab(H-a)(H-b)}{H(H-1)}\) and \(v(a,b)=(ab)^2+K(K-2ab)t_1+(2ab+K^2-4K+2)t_2+(4-2K)t_3+t_4-\mu(a,b)^2\). Then the exact finite null moments under independent fixed-row, equiprobable-site randomization are \(\mathbb E[C]=\binom{s}{2}^{-1}\sum_{i<j}\mu(r_i,r_j)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(C)=\binom{s}{2}^{-2}\sum_{i<j}v(r_i,r_j)\). Mutual independence need not hold for cycle edges: for three independent singleton species on two sites, every overlap is Bernoulli with mean \(1/2\), but the probability that all three overlaps equal one is \(1/4\), not \(1/8\). The moment formulas hold for arbitrary heterogeneous positive row sums and require neither sampling nor a normal approximation. They do not apply unchanged to fixed-column, column-proportional, or species-dependent site-selection nulls.
integrity: The forest product law follows from sequential leaf conditioning, independent of finite checks; the moment formula follows from hypergeometric falling-factorial expectations. Exact rational verification covers every pair-size case through 12 sites, plus 30,665 completely enumerated small matrices.
scientific_limitations: Applies only to independent fixed-row, equiprobable-column/site randomization. Column margins are not fixed, empty sites are permitted, and the result gives the first two null moments, not tail probabilities. Pairwise independence does not extend to all cyclic families.
title: Forest factorization gives exact finite null moments for the checkerboard score
